newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Euro/U.S. share markets hit new records.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Euro/U.S. share markets hit new records.

text.p: Investors went on a buying spree on Tuesday, sending several European bourses to record highs, while Wall Street, the world's top stock market, extended Monday's record-breaking performance.
London, Frankfurt, Amsterdam, Madrid and Budapest were among markets scaling new peaks and the Paris bourse advanced to its highest level since May 1994.
World oil prices also traded near six-year highs after an advance which has boosted them by 40 percent in four months.
On the foreign exchanges, the dollar hit a 33-month high against the yen and a four-month high versus the mark, while the pound was boosted by a rally in share prices and dearer oil.

Market analysts forecast more gains for European shares if a "dream combination" of steady economic growth and low inflation lasts, with investors likely to pump more cash in as prospects for corporate earnings and dividend payouts improve.
"The economic background is about as good as it gets," said Peter Sullivan, European equity strategist at U.S. investment bank Goldman Sachs in London.
But traders cautioned that investors might hold back a little ahead of British and U.S. statistics later in the week, particularly U.S. September consumer price (CPI) data on Wednesday.

On Monday, the Dow Jones industrial average ended above 6,000 for the first time, jumping 40.62 to 6,010. Healthy company earnings news helped it hit a new all-time high of 6,044.29 early on Tuesday before easing off a little.

"The question is how far do we go from here," said Peter Cardillo at Westfalia Investments in New York. "The market is going to go higher but I don't think the Dow can move much beyond the 6,100 level without a normal pullback."
The index of 30 U.S. blue-chip share prices has had a dizzying rise, soaring through 5,000 only last November, nine months after topping 4,000.

London's stock market, Europe's busiest, had already breached the 4,000 mark on the FTSE 100 share index and made further progress on Tuesday, supported by higher bonds and an agreed bid for international exhibitions group Blenheim.
"The market is in very good heart," said one senior trader. "Blenheim added fuel to the fire and the feeling is there are other bids still in the pipeline," another added.
Germany's DAX index opened at a record high above 2,700 and added to its gains, boosted by Wall Street's strength, higher bonds and a strong dollar -- good news for German exporters.

High oil prices weakened the yen, in view of Japan's dependence on imported oil, while helping to send the pound to 21-month highs against the mark, 11-month peaks versus the dollar and more than three-year highs against the yen.
"The general backdrop is definitely favouring the Anglo-Saxon currencies at the expense of core Europe and Japan," said Peter Von Maydell, senior currency economist at UBS.

London November futures for international benchmark North Sea Brent blend crude were down 13 cents a barrel at $24.73 in mid-afternoon, having earlier hit a new post-Gulf War high of $25.06 to add 20 cents to an 88 cent jump on Monday.
But despite the short-term boost dearer oil has given to various markets, economists and analysts said soaring oil prices could reignite dormant inflationary pressures.
CURRENCIES AT 1445 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.5395 marks and 112.30 yen, compared with 1.5293 and 111.60 in late European business on Monday. The pound gained to $1.5830 and 2.4370 marks from $1.5805 and 2.4174.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1445 GMT
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was up 18.2 points at 4,056.9, compared with an earlier record high of 4,063.2.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt ended bourse floor trade 34.57 ahead at 2,728.45, near its earlier peak of 2,728.64. It was around 2,722 in later electronic trade.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was 22.65 higher at 2,166.27 but below a year high around 2,176 hit earlier.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $381 an ounce in the afternoon, unchanged from the morning fix but below Monday's London close of $381.65. Silver was down four cents at $5.01.
